{{Quote|These gave as good as they got, and 'cold' and 'hot' wars alternated for a thousand years&mdash;while the Republic flagellated itself with inquisitions&mdash;until Pius Dea rule met its end in that famous encounter which hardly needs retelling here.|[[Gabrel Treon]], in his report ''[[Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji: A Cartel of Genes]]''|<ref name="TTSP">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/praji/20090205.html|text=Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji|int=Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji}}</ref>}}
The '''Inquisitions''' were special religious courts or tribunals held by the [[Pius Dea]]-controlled [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] around [[11,100 BBY]]. They were used to identify elements regarded as impure including heretics and apostates who were tried and executed in mass trials. Dissidents categorized as [[Proscribed]] were stripped of civil liberties, had their assets nationalized by the state, and their social mobility was severely limited. The Pius Dea sect also assigned commissars to Republic military units to root out opponents of the Pius Dea.<ref name="TEGtW" />

The Inquisitions were confined to the [[Colonies/Legends|Colonies]] and [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]], the core territories of the Republic. These developments led the [[Caamasi/Legends|Caamasi]] to successful persuade the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] to abandon their centuries-long [[Recusal]] and confront the Pius Dea. The Jedi collaborated with the Caamasi and [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakani]] to spread a heresy among the Pius Dea church which developed into the [[Renunciates|Renunciate]] movement by [[10,967 BBY]]. This anti-Pius Dea coalition which grew to include the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]], [[Herglic/Legends|Herglics]], and [[Duros/Legends|Duros]] planned to take over the Republic and [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] and remove the Pius Dea [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]]; goals which were accomplished during the [[Seventh Alsakan Conflict]].<ref name="TEGtW" />
